answer.summary_why: A traditional Jain wedding in Jaipur requires careful logistical planning for sunset dining and specific dietary compliance. My approach focuses on securing high-quality Jain catering early and ensuring the decor reflects the serene, regal aesthetic of a Jaipur sunset.

ideas.title: Jain-specialized menu tasting
ideas.description: Schedule a dedicated tasting session focusing on root-vegetable-free recipes like paneer, legumes, and seasonal fruits.
ideas.why: Ensures no onion, garlic, or root vegetables slip into the final spread.

ideas.title: Sunset-responsive lighting
ideas.description: Utilize warm, ambient fairy lights and lanterns that transition from soft daylight to evening elegance.
ideas.why: Perfectly complements the outdoor sunset dinner preference in Jaipur.

ideas.title: Digital-first guest logistics
ideas.description: Use a digital platform to track guest dietary needs and transport requirements in real-time.
ideas.why: Reduces printing costs and helps manage the 250-guest logistics efficiently.

budget_emphasis.why: Creating a delicious, high-end Jain menu requires specialized chefs and ingredients.
The sunset timing demands sophisticated lighting to look beautiful in photos.

extra_tasks.title: Verify no-root-veg sourcing with caterer
extra_tasks.why: Strict Jain dietary requirements need vendor validation well in advance.

extra_tasks.title: Confirm sunset timing for ceremony and dinner
extra_tasks.why: Jaipur February sunset times change; must align with ritual muhurtham.

vendor_notes.why: Must provide a written guarantee that no root vegetables (potatoes, onions, garlic) are used in any dish.
Ensure the muhurtham times are strictly aligned with the sunset dinner schedule.
Confirm if they have a dedicated kitchen area to ensure no cross-contamination of Jain food.
Ask them to scout the venue specifically for 'golden hour' lighting at the ceremony time.

answer.summary_why: We are focusing on a sustainable, alcohol-free celebration in Jaipur that prioritizes eco-friendly materials and traditional elegance. My approach ensures that the zero-plastic mandate is integrated into every vendor contract while keeping the logistics smooth for your 250 guests.

ideas.title: Eco-friendly floral mandap
ideas.description: Use only local, fresh marigolds and jasmine with bamboo structures instead of plastic foam or artificial drapes.
ideas.why: Fits the zero-plastic preference while looking authentic and beautiful in Jaipur.

ideas.title: Digital-first guest experience
ideas.description: Use QR codes for event schedules and menus instead of printed cards.
ideas.why: Reduces paper waste significantly and aligns with the sustainable theme.

ideas.title: Seed-paper return gifts
ideas.description: Gift guests small potted plants or items packaged in seed paper that can be planted.
ideas.why: A meaningful, zero-plastic gift that guests can take home.

ideas.title: Traditional Jaipur mocktail bar
ideas.description: Feature local sherbets and lassis served in clay kulhads.
ideas.why: Perfect for a dry wedding and eliminates plastic glass waste.

budget_emphasis.why: Since it is a dry wedding, investing more in high-quality, diverse food and artisanal non-alcoholic drinks is essential.
Sourcing plastic-free alternatives often requires more specialized craftsmanship and natural materials.

extra_tasks.title: Confirm zero-plastic policy with catering and decor vendors
extra_tasks.why: Crucial to ensure all disposables, straws, and packaging are strictly eco-friendly.

extra_tasks.title: Arrange eco-friendly waste management for the venue
extra_tasks.why: Ensures the event leaves no plastic footprint at the venue.

extra_tasks.title: Source clay kulhads for beverage service
extra_tasks.why: Traditional and plastic-free solution for beverage service.

vendor_notes.why: Must guarantee zero plastic in food serving, cutlery, and storage.
Check if they can provide natural fabric drapes and bamboo structures instead of plastic props.
Ask if they have existing partnerships with waste-management services to handle compostable waste.

answer.summary_why: Celebrating a traditional Bengali-style Durga Puja in Pune requires authentic cultural elements, careful noise management, and community-driven logistics.

ideas.title: Community dhunuchi competition
ideas.description: Host a dhunuchi dance competition for residents during the cultural program.
ideas.why: It is a central, high-energy tradition that fosters community engagement.

ideas.title: Community-cooked bhog
ideas.description: Involve resident volunteers to help prepare portions of the bhog in the society kitchen.
ideas.why: It reduces catering costs while strengthening the sense of community ownership.

ideas.title: Eco-friendly floral mandap
ideas.description: Use marigolds and banana leaves for a traditional, sustainable Bengali pandal look.
ideas.why: It keeps the aesthetic authentic to Bengali culture while minimizing waste in Pune's civic guidelines.

ideas.title: Shared waste responsibility
ideas.description: Assign volunteer 'green teams' to monitor waste segregation at the bhog counter.
ideas.why: It ensures compliance with municipal waste rules and saves on professional service fees.

budget_emphasis.why: High-quality, traditional Bengali idol and priest services are vital for the essence of the event.
Feeding 400 people high-quality authentic bhog is the primary expectation of a community Durga Puja.
Focusing on simple, elegant traditional decor allows for more budget for the rituals and meals.

extra_tasks.title: Source specialized Bengali incense and dhak players
extra_tasks.why: Essential for authentic atmosphere and often booked out early in Pune.

extra_tasks.title: Distribute bhog token system
extra_tasks.why: Manages crowd flow and ensures accurate food portions for 400 guests.

extra_tasks.title: Coordinate with neighbors regarding noise limits
extra_tasks.why: Proactive communication prevents complaints regarding cultural music and evening prayers.

vendor_notes.why: Ensure the idol matches the traditional Bengali style and uses water-soluble natural clay.
Specifically ask for experience in preparing traditional Bengali bhog including khichuri and labra.
Ensure they understand the specific bamboo-structure aesthetics typical of Bengali pandals.
Ask for low-decibel speakers to strictly comply with Pune's residential noise regulations.
Confirm they handle organic waste (leftover food) for composting as part of a 'Green' Ganeshotsav/Puja goal.
